# GNU.org

> GNU.org is the official home of the Free Software Foundation and GNU Project, dedicated to promoting software freedom, the four essential freedoms, and building free operating systems and software.

GNU.org serves as the central hub for the GNU Project and Free Software Movement, offering comprehensive resources on free software philosophy, licensing, software packages, and GNU/Linux distributions. The site emphasizes user freedom, copyleft principles, and community contribution to free and open-source software development.

## Key Topics

- Free Software
- GNU Project
- GNU/Linux
- Free Software Foundation (FSF)
- Software Freedom
- Four Essential Freedoms
- Copyleft
- GPL Licenses
- Richard Stallman

- User Freedom

- Linux Distributions
- Software Philosophy

## Core GNU Project

- [The GNU Operating System and the Free Software Movement](https://www.gnu.org): GNU project homepage defining free software movement and operating system.
- [About the GNU Operating System](https://www.gnu.org/gnu/gnu.html): Overview of GNU operating system history and project structure.
- [Software](https://www.gnu.org/software/software.html): Directory of GNU software packages and getting started guide.

## Philosophy and Freedoms

- [Philosophy of the GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/philosophy.html): GNU project philosophy covering four essential freedoms and copyleft.
- [What is Free Software?](https://www.gnu.org/philosophy/free-sw.html): Definition of free software and the four essential freedoms.
- [Proprietary Software](https://www.gnu.org/proprietary/proprietary.html): Analysis of proprietary software issues and free software advocacy.

## Licensing and Legal

- [Licenses](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/licenses.html): GNU licensing guide covering GPL, LGPL, and license compatibility.

## GNU/Linux Distributions

- [GNU/Linux Distros](https://www.gnu.org/distros/distros.html): GNU/Linux distribution guidelines and recommendations.
- [List of Free GNU/Linux Distributions](https://www.gnu.org/distros/free-distros.html): Endorsed GNU/Linux distributions meeting freedom guidelines.

## Documentation and Resources

- [Documentation of the GNU Project](https://www.gnu.org/doc/doc.html): Central documentation hub with manuals, guides, and contribution info.
- [Free Software and Education](https://www.gnu.org/education/education.html): Resources on free software adoption in educational institutions.
- [Audio/Video](https://www.gnu.org/audio-video/audio-video.html): GNU philosophy recordings, speeches, and hackers' meeting videos.
- [Recordings about GNU Philosophy and History](https://www.gnu.org/audio-video/philosophy-recordings.html): Video and audio recordings on GNU philosophy and free software.

## Community and Contribution

- [Helping the GNU Project and the Free Software Movement](https://www.gnu.org/help/help.html): Volunteer opportunities and ways to contribute to GNU project.
- [GNU's Who](https://www.gnu.org/people/people.html): Directory of GNU project contributors and package maintainers.

## Optional

- [The GNU Art Gallery](https://www.gnu.org/graphics/graphics.html): GNU logos, artwork gallery, and design guidelines.
- [Laugh along with GNU](https://www.gnu.org/fun/humor.html): Collection of GNU-related jokes and computing humor.
- [Site map of www.gnu.org](https://www.gnu.org/server/sitemap.html): Navigation index and directory structure of gnu.org website.
- [Hyper Estraier @ www.gnu.org](https://www.gnu.org/cgi-bin/estseek.cgi): Full-text search engine interface for gnu.org website.
